properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 14 at 4:33PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 432 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 9
miles west of Saguache, or 44 miles southeast of Gunnison, moving
east at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 40 to 50 mph, half inch hail and brief heavy
rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Saguache and Moffat.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 14 at 4:29PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
At 429 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking strong thunderstorms along
a line extending from 9 miles southwest of Pagosa Springs to 14 miles
east of Ignacio. Movement was east at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation and
outdoor objects is possible.

Locations impacted include...
Juanita, Pagosa Junction, Arboles, Gato, and Lonetree.

This includes the following highways...
U.S. Highway 84 in Colorado between mile markers 14 and 18.
Colorado 151 between mile markers 15 and 18.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 14 at 4:26PM MDT until September 14 at 5:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
SVRPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southeastern Baca County in southeastern Colorado...

* Until 500 PM MDT.

* At 425 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 11 miles south of
Stonington, or 16 miles northwest of Elkhart, moving northeast at
30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage
to roofs, siding, and trees.

* This severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly rural areas of
southeastern Baca County.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 14 at 4:11PM MDT until September 14 at 7:15PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Pitkin County in west central Colorado...

* Until 715 PM MDT.

* At 411 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Flash flooding is already
occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northwestern Pitkin County.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 14 at 2:04PM MDT until September 14 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows are possible, flooding
caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Ouray County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 600 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall is possible over the Gold Mountain
Burn Scar which could lead to flash flooding and/or debris flows,
particularly along highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter
Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 202 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in Gold Mountain Burn Scar.
- Gold Mountain Burn Scar is the most likely place to experience
minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Ouray.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
